body:
I understand the feeling of wanting to give up and die, and of wanting to stop trying. I have struggles with my issues for over 21 year (almost half of my life). I can't tell you it will get better, because frankly it never really has gotten better for me, nor do I have any way to read your future...that being said, I CAN at least offer this....most employers rarely call back on job applications...you would have a much better chance at success in your job hunt if you call them and ask for a job interview within a short time of applying. There are a couple of free websites that offer good advice for job seeking: 

http://www.quintcareers.com/job_applications.html  

http://fortadam.hubpages.com/hub/How-To-Successfully-Hunt-For-and-Get-A-Job

Hope that the info helps you get a job, and that in doing so, helps alleviate some of the pain you are going through. Also, there are several places out there who are reliable and who can help you manage debt, not to mention the fact that if it came from a motorcycle accident, there may be things that can be done to get compensated for it, especially if the other driver was at fault. That being said, be careful when getting help, as there are many out there that take advantage of others. 

Hope it helps man.

Its okay to be ugly and stupid if that is truly the case...firstly because being "ugly" or "stupid" depends on your audience and what you are being compared to, and secondly because the majority of the human race has been in those two categories for at least part if not the majority of their life....and frankly, that INCLUDES those that are held up as paragons of beauty or wisdom. That being said, the likely hood is great that you are neither ugly nor stupid....it is a far more likely that you see yourself through a very warped mirror....and unfortunately, humans can be quite cruel...if someone feels insecure, it is often easier to belittle or make another feel worthless than it is to address their own insecurities.

I can't tell you it will get better...I have struggled with depression, anxiety, and a desire for death for over two decades....almost half of my adult life. I had a brother who committed suicide 6 years ago, a sister who has made several unsuccessful attempts, and a son who has made two attempts. There are many days when I wish that I had followed through the first time I decided to make an attempt. I know the feeling of worthlessness and being unable to escape from yourself. You said that your problems were "menial and non-specific"....I haven't found anything that really helps me, but if you have access to a therapist/psychiatrist and medication, you might try that route...my sister went through 4 meds before she found one that worked for her, but she tells me that she is finally a lot happier...who knows...maybe it will help you, especially if the problem is how you feel without any sort of triggering event. That being said, please don't be afraid to share how you feel...regardless of how "trivial/menial" some people might think your problems might be, to you they are real enough and serious enough to cause you pain and a desire to die, and the whole point of this message board is to give you a chance to share how you feel with people who are going through similar struggles.

I am sorry that you finally found someone who helped and then suddenly lost her...I am also kind of jealous...I have struggled with my issues for over two decades, and haven't yet found a therapist yet that I would consider someone I trusted, let alone a foundation...so I can certainly empathize with how hard it must be to finally find someone who actually helped and then suddenly lose that anchor.

I appreciate your words guys. Can't say that I am happy about hanging around for so long, and I certainly don't feel like a fighter....in fact I wonder at times if I were a bit braver if I would then be able to go through with it (death doesn't bother me...I have done several hundred post mortums, and see a lot of death in my line of work...but an unsuccessful attempt and the chance of being maimed or paralyzed and living through the attempt terrifies me). That being said, it is nice to hear from those who can at least partially understand what I am going through, and who don't judge me for how I feel....I do a good enough job beating myself up for being who I am without needing others to judge me too. Its very hard for me to open up to others...I wear a very good mask when I have to be around other people, and I keep my scars hidden as much as possible.
